summary: Backend: 17/17 pytest tests passed for auth, ready stock, beginning balance, image upload (Emergent storage), cash book, profit-loss, balance-sheet, summary. Frontend: All flows pass after fixing a critical AuthContext bug. Login → dashboard → all 6 nav links → CRUD on beginning balance, ready stock, cash book → P&L, balance sheet, logout all work end-to-end.

minor.issue: Possible accounting model limitation: inventory added via ready-stock without offsetting cash purchase transaction produces UNBALANCED state (aktiva > pasiva). modal field only reflects beginning balance and laba_ditahan only reflects sold items. Adding unsold inventory or income-only transactions creates imbalance. Not a bug per se but worth documenting.

ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL: useEffect used `active` cleanup flag together with `checkedRef` guard, which under React.StrictMode (enabled in index.js) caused the initial /auth/me request's .finally(setLoading(false)) to be skipped: 1st mount fires request, cleanup sets active=false, 2nd mount early-returns due to checkedRef (no new request), original promise resolves but active=false → loading remained true forever → entire app stuck on 'Memuat...' after login. FIXED by removing the active flag.

action_items: Review the AuthContext fix in /app/frontend/src/context/AuthContext.js (removed active flag) and decide on a more robust StrictMode-safe pattern (e.g., use AbortController or rely solely on checkedRef without active flag).

Optional accounting fix: when creating a ready-stock item, consider auto-creating a corresponding cash-book expense transaction (or adjusting balance-sheet logic) so neraca naturally balances; currently neraca shows UNBALANCED whenever there is unsold inventory not represented in beginning balance.
critical_code_review_comments: AuthContext mixed `checkedRef` + `active` cleanup is a StrictMode anti-pattern – pick ONE (ref guard OR active flag), not both, otherwise the pending request's resolution is silently dropped.
server.py upload_image reads entire file into memory before size check — for large files this still consumes memory; consider streaming or relying on multipart limits.
server.py: profit_loss is called twice from balance_sheet and summary (no caching). Minor perf concern.
Single 600-line backend file is acceptable now but should be split (routers/auth, routers/stock, routers/cash, services) as it grows.
Backend has no rate limiting / brute force lockout on /auth/login (playbook recommends lockout after 5 fails).

context_for_next_testing_agent: AuthContext had a StrictMode + checkedRef + active cleanup bug that caused the post-login UI to remain on 'Memuat...' forever. I removed the `active` flag (kept `checkedRef`). All backend pytest at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py pass (17/17). Frontend smoke covered: login, all 6 nav links, beginning-balance save (total Rp 6.000.000), ready-stock create, cash-book create with running balance (closing Rp 6.800.000), profit-loss (net Rp 0), balance-sheet (renders aktiva/pasiva + balance-status), logout. Balance sheet shows UNBALANCED when inventory/transactions are added without an offsetting cash purchase — likely an accounting model design issue rather than a code bug.
rca of the issue: RCA: src/context/AuthContext.js had `useEffect(() => { if (checkedRef.current) return; checkedRef.current = true; let active = true; api.get('/auth/me')...finally(() => active && setLoading(false)); return () => { active = false; }; }, [])`. Under React 18 StrictMode in dev, the effect mounts→cleanup→mounts again. On first mount the request fires; cleanup sets active=false; on second mount checkedRef is already true so the function early-returns WITHOUT firing a new request and WITHOUT setting active=true again. When the original /auth/me promise resolves, `active && setLoading(false)` evaluates to false and setLoading is never called, leaving `loading=true` forever. Therefore ProtectedRoute always renders the 'Memuat...' fallback after navigation to '/'. Reproduction: open /login, login successfully – URL becomes '/' but only 'MEMUAT…' shows. Mitigation applied: removed the `active` cleanup flag in AuthContext.js so setLoading(false) always runs after /auth/me resolves; `checkedRef` continues to prevent double requests.
